title: Ledger record: dispatch preflight
description: The clarify-then-commit gate's briefing (issue #67, task t14): the operating facts a dispatch depends on, composed by the engine from the actor's ADVERTISED host capabilities plus the task declaration, and handed over before the actor's first billable turn. It generalizes deploy/prod/install-secrets.sh's single-use windowed confirmation from danger to understanding, and keeps that protocol's load-bearing properties: the document is composed at `verdict: hold`, it states what does not proceed and why, and it expires. It carries `derived` authority and nothing else -- it is a deterministic function of state nobody in this record asserted, which is exactly what makes it derivable; the ledger append layer refuses every other authority for this type (RulePreflightDerivedOnly). The host block is the BRIDGE's own advertisement, copied verbatim: the engine states who said it and when, and never re-renders or supplements a fact it did not measure.

data.$comment: Unlike the Phase 0 record types, the core fields are required rather than documentary: a preflight that states no facts would refuse a dispatch in order to tell the actor nothing.

verdict.description: Always `hold` on a composed preflight, exactly like the confirmation file's default verdict line. Composing a briefing never authorizes anything; the acknowledgement is a separate action by a different party, recorded as its own `dispatch_acknowledgement` record.

protocol_version.description: The gate protocol version the control plane composed this document under.

capability_protocol_version.description: The version of the capability surface the bridge advertised, as the bridge stated it. Recorded beside the gate's own version because they can legitimately differ.

task.description: The task declaration half of the composition: what the engine knows about the dispatch this preflight is for. Every field comes from the pinned definition or the run's own state -- nothing here is supplied by the actor being briefed.

actor_key.description: The actor identity the reference resolves to.

actor_id.description: The actors-table row id, present only when the registry could answer. Absent means unattributed, never a fabricated id.

workflow_digest.description: The immutable definition this run pinned, so an acknowledgement is against a graph that cannot have changed since.

deadline.description: The attempt deadline, when the node declares one. Absent means the node declared none.

host_capabilities.description: The bridge's advertised host facts, verbatim -- which sandbox modes actually work on this host, the commit/harvest policy in force for the lane, which paths the task may write, and whatever else the backend measured. Deliberately unconstrained: the facts are backend-specific while the protocol is not, and a typed shape here would either constrain four backends to one backend's idea of a host or drift into a union of everything. An empty object is a real answer -- a bridge whose facts went missing between registration and dispatch says so rather than having content invented for it.

expected_result.description: What `done` must look like for the operator to accept this dispatch.

outcomes.description: The domain outcomes the node's contract declares.

acknowledgement.description: How the reader commits the second, separate action. Both a verb and an endpoint are stated because the two readers differ: a human or an operator agent reaches for the verb, a bridge for the endpoint.

verdict.description: The verdict an acknowledgement carries to commit the dispatch.

refusal.description: What does not proceed, and why -- the property inherited from the destructive-confirmation file, which names what breaks rather than merely asking for a keystroke. It states that the actor has not been invoked, that the acknowledgement is single-use, and when the window closes.

expires_at.description: When this preflight stops being acknowledgeable. A stale briefing must not authorize today's dispatch -- the same reason the confirmation-file protocol is windowed.
